descriptions.title: What a covering design actually is (and is not)
descriptions.body: A covering design is a set of k-number tickets chosen so that every t-subset of your chosen pool appears on at least one ticket. The guarantee is purely combinatorial: IF at least t of your pool numbers happen to be drawn, THEN at least one ticket is guaranteed to show a t-match. This restructures HOW your tickets overlap the combination space - it does not change the per-ticket odds and cannot predict a draw. Lottery Wiz states this everywhere, including inside the AI's own system prompt, because the whole point of the tool is honest structure, not false hope. gen_wheel (Fantasy 5) and wheel (any game) implement it as a greedy maximum-coverage selection.

descriptions.title: Two engines, one contract
descriptions.body: engine_py.py is the deep Fantasy-5 engine with N=42, PICK=5 baked in and a single rich draw store. lottery_general.py is the generalized engine: every function takes (N, k) and an optional bonus pool (Bn, b), with a PRESETS registry of real games and per-game draw stores. The split keeps the F5 app fast and faithful to Renne's original research while letting any other lottery reuse the same backtest / ledger / curated-builder ideas. Critically, Fantasy5/engine.js mirrors engine_py so the browser page runs offline, and mcp_server.py imports engine_py directly - so the math is identical across the server, the browser, and Claude Desktop.

descriptions.title: The Brutal Ledger and its exact random control
descriptions.body: ledger_run replays a FIXED ticket set across every historical draw with real payout math, returning net P/L, ROI, an equity curve, a per-tier histogram, the best single-draw payout and the worst losing streak. Tickets and draws are encoded as integer bitmasks so each match count is a single popcount (bit_count), making thousands of draws cheap. The honest counterweight is montecarlo_control: because a uniformly-random ticket's match count against any fixed draw has the SAME hypergeometric distribution by symmetry, an entire random-quick-pick run reduces to ONE multinomial draw over n_tickets*n_draws trials. NumPy makes 2,000 control runs take microseconds, and percentile_of reports exactly where your strategy lands versus pure luck - usually the blunt truth that it didn't beat random.

descriptions.title: The curated 'Build My Play Set' funnel
descriptions.body: build_play_set is a transparent six-stage pipeline whose every count is shown to the user: the full C(N,5) space -> reduce to your pool -> drop combinations that already occurred in history -> drop is_edge() shapes (all-consecutive, all-odd/even, all-low/high, arithmetic progressions, range<=6 clusters, extreme sums) -> rank survivors by profile_score (a gaussian peak at the ~107 sum hotzone, odd/even and low/high near 2-3, zero consecutive, spread, and novelty versus recent draws) -> coverage-aware greedy top-N that maximises pair/triple coverage while keeping profile high. It scores SHAPE, not likelihood; the Universal version (build_curated + derive_profile) learns the profile from each game's own history instead of using Fantasy-5 constants.

descriptions.title: Local-first AI with a no-paid-API path
descriptions.body: Ask Wiz defaults to local Ollama models (auto-detected, embeddings filtered) and streams tokens as Server-Sent Events; a cloud model is used only when a key is configured. Crucially the AI does not invent numbers: when asked to build something it emits a fenced 'lotterywiz' action block that the UI parses and executes by driving the real controls, so the AI's result is byte-identical to pressing the buttons. Four per-app system prompts (Fantasy 5, Universal, Super Sete, Scratch) shape its behaviour, and the preferred zero-cost route is the MCP server, which lets Claude Desktop call the same engine over the subscription with no per-token billing.

descriptions.title: Honest data, official where possible
descriptions.body: Fantasy 5 history is built from the official Georgia Lottery API (latest draw only) plus lottonumbers.com year archives (cross-validated) for backfill - 4,222 draws from 2015 to mid-2026. The Universal games pull from official feeds where they exist: data.ny.gov Socrata (Powerball/Mega Millions/Cash4Life), the Caixa API (eight Brazilian games, with month-name and trevo bonus parsing), and FDJ open data (France Loto), plus an EuroMillions community API. Where no reliable free source exists (SuperEnalotto, EuroJackpot, UK Lotto, Lotto 6/49; Powerball/EuroMillions jackpots) the app says so plainly and falls back to CSV import rather than fabricating data.
